correctness.rationale: Stationary Fourier generator yields an inductive finite triangular moment system with strictly positive denominators at degree at least one. Exact radial moments through sixth order give the two cumulant formulas. The sixth-numerator quadratic has positive constant and strictly negative g and g-squared coefficients, and substitution at the previously published fourth zero gives -8(2d+1)(3d+1)(4d+3)<0, proving unique ordered thresholds for all d>0. At the fourth zero the exact sixth cumulant is strictly negative. The independent translational Gaussian component contributes no cumulant above order two. A standalone checker reconstructs the symbolic identities and verifies exact-rational linear generator systems at five parameter pairs; sampling is auxiliary to universal algebra.

originality.rationale: The exact same-model article (Santra–Basu–Sabhapandit, arXiv:2107.12640) already publishes the fourth-order transition, which is explicitly excluded from the novelty claim. The new result derives the full sixth projected cumulant, proves a unique sixth-order zero strictly earlier than the fourth-order zero for all strictly positive rotational diffusivities, and shows the sixth cumulant is uniformly negative along the whole known zero-kurtosis locus. Material of the same-model primary article, including Appendix A, and full text of two plausible nearby active-particle papers was compared. Published-record and prior-literature checks did not identify an equivalent sixth-order phase classification. General moment recurrences make implicit derivability a real remaining risk; search absence is not proof of priority.
residual_risks: Earlier general generator methodology algebraically permits the sixth moment; the same result could have been derived elsewhere but omitted or indexed under another terminology.
Published literature search is not exhaustive, and publication-priority certainty is not claimed.

value.rationale: The primary same-model literature emphasizes that fourth cumulant zero does not imply a Gaussian distribution. The new explicit sixth cumulant rules out Gaussianity uniformly on that entire physically motivated zero-kurtosis line and reveals two distinct higher-order sign crossovers for every diffusion ratio. This is a natural, global and sharp classification with a robust invariance to added thermal noise; not an arbitrary parameter slice, minor numerical precision gain, or a claim about morphology.
